learning.title: Shard the web shell browser lane per project and keep the auth chain whole
learning.trigger: Sharding or re-balancing full / web shell browser, or adding a spec that reads the bootstrapped API.
learning.mistake: One Playwright --shard over desktop and mobile cuts contiguous chunks: desktop shell tests (2713 test-seconds) landed in two shards and mobile in the others, a 4.5x spread, and it can split the serial desktop-auth-bootstrap then desktop-shared-admin chain or leave real-api.spec.ts on an unbootstrapped database where it skips.
learning.rule: Slice desktop and mobile separately with --project and --shard=i/N, run the auth chain whole in one shard first, seed the bootstrap admin with web-auth-seed.ts in every other shard, and list the unsharded suite in each shard so all 22 core cases are proven listed once. Give each shard its own database, API and ports. Keep the amd runner label, which names the heavy-lane pool; Intel hosts ran the lane 1.76x slower and timed out, and two of the four runners are Intel, so budget for them (heavy-lane-label-is-pool-not-cpu). Register every shard as its own job name and lane id in required-checks.json, because verify-run.ts needs each policy job exactly once.

verification.requirement: playwright test --list per shard, unioned with the chain projects, equals the unsharded list with no duplicates.
